chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Could Louis Armstrong read? Erskine Tate's Vendome pit band
summary: They discuss the reading demands of theater pit work with Erskine Tate and doubt a story about Armstrong's music being marked.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: That's (unintelligible) down in the pit. That's right.
Yeah, you did. Erskine (unintelligible), Erskine had a very good band (unintelligible). in the Vendome Theater

I think Louie could read, but not as good as them fellows like Bob Shoffner, all them fellows like that, you know, like Buster, because they was playing -- you know, at that time with them big pictures they have the score to go with it.
That's right. You had to read it.

Because you had his cello, violin. He had clarinet. He had Buster on clarinet, and he had this other fellow, Cuban fellow on clarinet. Jimmy Bertrand was on drums. Jimmy and I went to school together.

But, you know, this thing, this story that when he came to fill in Fletcher, that got music marked (unintelligible) Louie doesn't go down soft at all. He blowing out loud didn't just (unintelligible), and they say (unintelligible) you see (the marked ? What do you think "pp" stands for what) music was not. It's a way (unintelligible), and he said
I mean I don't know whether I suppose Fletcher's band was a little advanced perhaps compared to what he'd been doing.
I mean that was a band (unintelligible), wasn't it?
Because that's right, because, now, he worked with Carroll Charles Dickerson, and he (unintelligible). All those bands played music. They had to read it, and in that pit they had to read something.
Yeah, I think that story about Louie must be really a bit of an invention.
